questions.q: What does the summary say a typical meal should look like?
a: Plenty of vegetables alongside a modest serving of lean protein
A large portion of pasta with a small portion of vegetables
Equal portions of carbohydrates, fats and proteins
A small salad followed by a serving of dessert
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes a typical plate as mostly vegetables with only a modest serving of lean protein such as chicken.

questions.q: How often does Giada suggest limiting desserts and alcohol?
questions.why: Lesson 1 sets a limit of twice per week for desserts and alcohol when building a healthier plate.

questions.q: Why does Giada recommend precooking components at the start of the week?
a: It makes improvising quick, healthy meals much easier
It removes the need to ever cook during the week
It keeps vegetables fresh for longer in the fridge
It allows you to skip breakfast without feeling hungry
questions.why: Lesson 2 says precooked ingredients let you assemble a salad, grain bowl or meat and vegetable dish in under five minutes.

questions.q: How much dairy does the book suggest eating daily?
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends consuming just half a cup of dairy each day.

questions.q: Besides nutrition, which two parts of a healthy lifestyle does the book stress?
questions.why: Lesson 3 says regular exercise and supplements that address vitamin deficiencies are the other essential parts of a healthy lifestyle.
